# Retain only HTTP/1 terminator buffer reuse

Baseline: 23ec7c87a55c6c53043b5fc59befda627b08c560.
The user requests keeping only justified parts of PR7. Remove shared routing/header and H2 changes; retain only the H1 no-trailer buffer reuse and its one-byte pipelining regression test. Other candidates are deferred, not diagnosed as regressions.

Validate the exact reduced source with workspace checks and independent Linux protocol clients. Measure baseline/candidate H1 terminal-chunk allocations and wire output, and an uninstrumented focused timing comparison including no-trailer, trailers and fixed-length controls. Run exactly ten alternating pairs per workload, 20 seconds at 64 VUs after eight-iteration preflights, in a fixed paired k6 H1 comparison including plaintext, streaming and verified TLS streaming. Use existing 3% throughput/CPU and5% tail margins, record failures and all observations; do not repeat to obtain a pass. Unchanged H2/shared sources must equal baseline. Keep previous bundle findings in history/evidence, clearly separated from the retained candidate; do not reuse its passing results as qualification of this new exact build.

reproduction.pod.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: maximus-perf-h1-retained
  labels:
    purpose: temporary-maximus-benchmark
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: measure
  namespace: maximus-perf-h1-retained
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/hostname: homelab-01
  restartPolicy: Never
  activeDeadlineSeconds: 7200
  volumes:
    - name: work
      emptyDir: {}
  containers:
    - name: server
      image: rust:1.96-bookworm
      command: [sh, -c, 'mkdir -p /work/results; chmod 777 /work/results; sleep 7200']
      resources:
        requests: {cpu: '2', memory: 4Gi}
        limits: {cpu: '2', memory: 6Gi}
      securityContext:
        seccompProfile: {type: Unconfined}
      volumeMounts:
        - {name: work, mountPath: /work}
    - name: client
      image: grafana/k6:1.6.0
      command: [sh, -c, 'sleep 7200']
      resources:
        requests: {cpu: '2', memory: 1Gi}
        limits: {cpu: '2', memory: 2Gi}
      volumeMounts:
        - {name: work, mountPath: /work}

reproduction_instructions:
Use an isolated checkout of baseline 23ec7c87a55c6c53043b5fc59befda627b08c560. Extract the shared reproduction keys and probe_lock.content from the historical manifest at d792d98a1cda02e8f65a6d36868f2fceb424c5b5 into artifacts/lean-ownership/. Verify the recorded SHA-256 values. Extract this manifest's reproduction files into artifacts/h1-retained/. Copy the historical server.rs, pin.rs and http2-timing-wrapper.rs there; write the historical probe_lock.content to probe-linux.lock. Apply this manifest's patch to the current checkout, leaving the git-archived baseline untouched. build.py recreates that baseline and writes retained.rs before constructing the two focused binaries. Use Rust 1.96.0 on macOS ARM64; prime the registry cache before its --offline builds. Run micro.py, then summarize.py micro.

On Linux x86-64 apply the embedded pod.yaml to a disposable namespace, adapting only its hostname selector to the measurement node. It records the actual requests/limits, shared volume, deadline and server seccomp setting needed for io_uring. Its startup creates /work/results; make /work writable by the client too (chmod 777 /work). Use Rust 1.96.1 and an isolated /work directory with the archived baseline and the same extracted tools. Copy retained.rs and the shared Cargo cache before build-remote.py. The builder uses identical paths and lockfiles, normal-allocator timing and a separate instrumented executable, and emits source/binary/rlib identities. Run micro.py --remote with an otherwise idle measurement task; collect its micro.csv and allocations.json under the -linux names locally. Run summarize.py micro-linux. A/A is a byte copy, not a separate build.

For sockets use grafana/k6:1.6.0 and the recorded images on the same shared host, with a writable /work shared between server and client. Copy historical load.js to /work/load.js. Start historical client-loop.sh in the client, then load.py in the server. CPU masks 4 and 80 mean server CPU2 and client CPUs4/6; verify they are separate physical cores on the chosen host. build-remote.py generates a fresh localhost certificate and static/glibc pin launchers. The controller starts and terminates its own server per trial, validates readiness, uses verified TLS, and stops on any invalid run. Do not reuse a results directory: its 6 preflights and 60 timed trials must run once under the predefined plan. Copy socket.csv and run summarize.py socket. Record all raw logs and host/image identities before removing only the temporary namespace. Never publish the generated private key.
